title: 2023年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 One of my bad habits is saying "busy" when people ask me how I'm doing. Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn't drive better results. Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time?

P2 In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing.

P3 That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress, then they're probably a big deal. This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout(精疲力竭).

P4 Personally, I'm going to stop saying "busy" when people ask me how I am. It sounds self- righteous(自以为是的) and sets the wrong tone. Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off.

P5 That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.

questions.q: What is a reason for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy" when asked how he is doing?
options: He just follows successful people's example.
He is actually proud to be fully occupied.
He thinks everyone should be devoted to work.
He believes busyness ensures accomplishments.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is a reason for the author to be in the habit 问一个具体可在原文找到的原 因，答案直接落在某句话里。

【拆句】主干是 What is a reason，后接 for 引导的逻辑主语 for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy"，再用 when 状语 when asked how he is doing 限定情境。结构清晰，无 陷阱，只需读成“作者在被问近况时爱说忙，原因是什么”。 46. What is a reason for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy" when asked how he is doing? A) He just follows successful people's example. B) He is actually proud to be fully occupied. C) He thinks everyone should be devoted to work. D) He believes busyness ensures accomplishments.

【定位】Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. 有时是因为我确实忙，但另一些时候是因为那是我以为自己应该说的话。重要人物就这么 说，得到晋升的人就这么说。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say ↔ follows successful people's example 预判“效仿成功者的做法”与 He just follows successful people's example 完全吻合， 故锁定此项。 B) 张冠李戴 原文末尾反问 why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are 是带反思的反 问，并非作者承认自己“为忙而自豪”，选项把反问当作者的真实态度，属张冠李戴。 C) 无中生有 原文从未说作者认为“人人都应投身工作”；相反作者反思忙碌文化，everyone should be devoted to work 在文中无任何依据，属无中生有。 D) 与原文相反 原文明说 working long hours doesn't drive better results，即忙碌并不保证成就； busyness ensures accomplishments 与原文意思正好相反。 我们为什么倾向于认为忙碌的人地位高? A) 我们的地位可归因于我们的社会流动性。 B) 我们坚信努力工作会带来成功。 C) 我们自己的成功机会从来都不容易获得。 D) 我们发现很少有地位高的人有时间休闲。

questions.q: Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status?
options: Our status can be attributed to our social mobility.
We hold the belief that hard work leads to success.
Our own opportunity for success never comes easily.
We find few people of high status have time for leisure.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status 问的是原文研究已 经给出的解释，属可定位的明确事实。

【拆句】Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status 中 think 后接 that 宾语 从句 busy people are of high status。tend to 是“倾向于”，不是绝对，读时不必纠结，整 句即“我们为什么倾向认为忙人地位高”。 47. Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status? A) Our status can be attributed to our social mobility. B) We hold the belief that hard work leads to success. C) Our own opportunity for success never comes easily. D) We find few people of high status have time for leisure.

【定位】In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing. 换句话说，我们越是相信一个人靠努力工作就有成功的机会，就越倾向于认为那些放弃休 闲、一直工作的人地位更高。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说我们对社会流动的信念影响了地位判断，并非“地位可归因于社会流动”；status can be attributed to our social mobility 把“信念影响判断”偷换成“地位源于流动”，颠 倒了关系。 B) ✓ 正确 the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work ↔ We hold the belief that hard work leads to success 预判的“努力工作通向成功的信念”与 hold the belief that hard work leads to success 逐字对应，故锁定此项。 C) 无中生有 原文谈的是“相信有机会成功”，从未说“我们自己的成功机会来之不易”；opportunity for success never comes easily 在文中无依据，属无中生有。 D) 答非所问 题问“为何觉得忙人地位高”，few people of high status have time for leisure 是描述 高地位者的现象，没回答原因，且原文也未这么说，属答非所问兼无中生有。 从最近的一项研究中,我们对忙碌文化了解到什么? A) 它使员工陷入无休止的会议、邮件和压力之中。 B) 它迫使约20%的员工表现得总是很忙。 C) 它扭曲了许多员工对什么是满意生活的信念。 D) 它对许多忙碌员工的幸福感造成很大伤害。

questions.q: What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study?
options: It places employees in endless meetings, emails and stress.
It compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy.
It distorts many employees' belief of what a satisfying life is.
It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study 问一项研究 的具体结论，答案在原文摆着。

【拆句】What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study：主干 What do we learn，about 短语限定话题，from 短语点明信息来源。三段修饰平铺，无陷阱。 48. What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study? A) It places employees in endless meetings, emails and stress. B) It compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy. C) It distorts many employees' belief of what a satisfying life is. D) It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being.

【定位】This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout(精疲力竭). 这种忙碌文化正使员工难以找到工作与生活的平衡。根据近期一项研究，每五名高投入员工 中就有一名面临精疲力竭的风险。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 meetings, emails and stress 出自上一段对“显得忙的人”的描写 knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress，并非“近期研究”的结论；题问研究发现什么，此项把别 处内容搬来，属张冠李戴。 B) 偷换概念 原文 one in five（约20%）指的是“面临精疲力竭风险”的人，compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy 把这20%偷换成“被迫显得忙”，数据所指对象 被改。 C) 无中生有 原文未提忙碌文化“扭曲了员工对满意生活的认知”；distorts…belief of what a satisfying life is 在文中找不到对应句，属无中生有。 D) ✓ 正确 one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout ↔ It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being 预判“危害员工身心”与 does much harm to many busy employees' well-being 吻 合，故锁定此项。 根据作者的说法,像"我查看邮件的机会有限"这样的话听起来像什么? A) 某人太忙而无法及时查看所有邮件。 B) 某人反对当前盛行的工作文化。 C) 某人被环境所迫而停止工作。 D) 某人只是在享受他们的休息时间。

questions.q: What do such utterances as "I have limited access to email" sound like according to the author?
options: One is too busy to check all emails in time.
One is opposed to the prevailing work culture.
One is forced by circumstances to stop working.
One is simply enjoying their time off work.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do such utterances as … sound like according to the author 问作者认为这 类话听起来像什么，答案是原文作者的明确评价。

【拆句】What do such utterances as "I have limited access to email" sound like according to the author：such…as 举例结构，sound like 是“听起来像”。注意 sound like 后省略了表 语，正是要补的答案；according to the author 提示以作者原话为准。 49. What do such utterances as "I have limited access to email" sound like according to the author? A) One is too busy to check all emails in time. B) One is opposed to the prevailing work culture. C) One is forced by circumstances to stop working. D) One is simply enjoying their time off work.

【定位】Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off. “我邮件查看受限”“我一回来就回复”这类话听起来像是你被违背意愿地拦着不让工作，而不 是在充分利用你的休假时光。

【选项】A) 答非所问 题问这类话“听起来像”什么（即给人的印象），too busy to check all emails in time 描述的是字面情境而非作者说的负面印象；作者的重点是“像被迫”，此项答非所问。 B) 过度推断 作者只说这类话“听起来像被迫”、设错了基调，并未说它表示“反对主流工作文化”； opposed to the prevailing work culture 是读者强行拔高，属过度推断。 C) ✓ 正确 you're being held against your will from working ↔ One is forced by circumstances to stop working 预判“被迫无法工作”与 forced by circumstances to stop working 吻合，故锁定此项。 D) 与原文相反 原文用 as opposed to 把“被迫不能工作”与“充分享受休假”对立，明说这类话听起来 “不是”在享受休假；simply enjoying their time off work 恰是被否定的那一面，正好 相反。 作者和他的同事为什么推出"不在办公室邮件生成器"? A) 使忙碌的员工能够花更少的时间查看邮件。 B) 确保员工和雇主都真正拥有休息时间。 C) 阻止管理者谈论他们的团队通常有多忙。 D) 鼓励雇主和员工都及时回复邮件。

questions.q: Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator?
options: To enable busy employees to spend less time checking emails.
To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off.
To stop managers from talking about how busy their teams usually are.
To encourage both employers and employees to answer emails promptly.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator 问一个具体动作的目的，答案藏在原文相应段落。

【拆句】Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator：主 干 Why did the author and his colleagues launch，宾语是专有工具名。一般疑问语序无 陷阱，落脚在“为何推出这个工具”。 50. Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator? A) To enable busy employees to spend less time checking emails. B) To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off. C) To stop managers from talking about how busy their teams usually are. D) To encourage both employers and employees to answer emails promptly.

【定位】That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same. 这就是我们最近推出“Out of Office Email Generator”这款免费工具的原因，你可以在下个 长周末或出行前使用它。你可以大方而自豪地宣告，回来之前不会查邮件。管理者需要三 思，别在周末给团队发邮件、别炫耀自己多忙。领导者应自己带头休假，并鼓励员工同样 如此。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 “少花时间查邮件”只是手段、且只覆盖员工一方，原文目的是让双方“真正休假”；spend less time checking emails 把整体目的缩成局部手段，属以偏概全。 B) ✓ 正确 You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back ↔ To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same ↔ employers as well as employees 预判“让员工和雇主都真正休假”与 employees as well as employers truly have time off 完整对应、双方都覆盖，故锁定此项。 C) 以偏概全 “别谈论团队多忙”只是原文对管理者诸多建议之一 talking about how busy they are， 不是推出工具的总目的；stop managers from talking about how busy… 拿一个分支 当全部，属以偏概全。 D) 与原文相反 原文呼吁休假时“不查/不发邮件”，answer emails promptly（及时回邮件）与原文意图 正好相反。
